title: review: Active path 2: tool_disclosure active passes the minimal allowlist to Claude workers, with a bus-event escalation when a hidden tool is needed (v3)
spec:
Today (T-0802) tool_disclosure mode "active" is treated as shadow. Build the real active branch. Facts: spawn.run_worker builds the per-role Claude Code allowlist from the table at spawn.py:24-31 and passes it to the worker launch; tool_catalog.minimal_set(task, role) returns keep/drop/mandatory; Codex executors are untouched (their tools are the CLI's).
Do:
1. Active: when promotion.mode("tool_disclosure") == "active", run_worker passes the minimal set's `keep` list (mandatory always included) as the allowlist for review, spec_review, scout, challenge and the Claude execute fallback; the legacy full list is still logged in the tool_disclosure decision row as candidates, and the decision's selected becomes the kept list.
2. Escalation path (P11): the worker prompt gains one line telling the worker that if it needs a tool outside its allowlist it must post `bus_post_result` with status "held" and reason starting "needs_tool:<tool id>"; daemon (or spawn.run_worker's result handling) recognises that reason, records a decision_log row kind "tool_disclosure" reason "hidden_tool_requested", and re-spawns the worker once with the full legacy allowlist (respawn capped at one per task; the second attempt logs "tool_escalation_used" in the task pipeline). Scorecard: hidden_tool_recovery_rate per role = escalations / active spawns; `scorecard --economy` shows it.
3. Safety: mandatory tools (Read for all, Bash(git *) for review/scout, tests-green + Edit/Write for execute, bus_post_result for all) can never be dropped; a docs-only execute keeps Edit/Write.
Tests: tests/test_spawn.py::test_active_allowlist_is_minimal_set_with_mandatory, ::test_hidden_tool_request_respawns_once_with_full_allowlist; tests/test_tool_catalog.py::test_mandatory_never_dropped_in_active; docs/context-economy/06-tool-disclosure.md Active section with the revert path.
Do not ask questions; decide and note decisions in the result. Never quote double-brace placeholder tokens literally.

SPEC v2 (2026-09-23 03:35) after spec review T-0908 (request_changes), binding on top of v1:
- The escalation respawn is synchronous inside spawn.run_worker: after run_claude returns, a helper `_hidden_tool_request(task_id)` reads bus.get(task_id) and returns the tool id when the worker posted status "held" with a reason starting "needs_tool:"; run_worker calls it BEFORE the generic done/failed post_result branches for every role (mirroring the existing review-role guard), and on a hit runs run_claude once more with the full legacy allowlist, then continues with the normal result handling of that second run. orchestrator/daemon.py leaves the scope; no daemon retry path is added.
- Budget and timeout for the second attempt come out of the original reservation: max_budget_usd for the retry = original cap minus the first attempt's spend (from its usage/usd), timeout = original timeout minus elapsed; when either remainder is below 10% of the original the respawn is skipped and the task is held with reason "needs_tool:<id> (no budget for respawn)" for the Planner. No second pool.reserve().
- hidden_tool_recovery_rate is a key inside context_scorecard.build()'s existing by_role_task_class rows (escalations / active spawns for that row), so `scorecard --economy` shows it without touching cli.py; cli.py stays out of scope.
- tests/test_spawn.py::test_hidden_tool_request_respawns_once_with_full_allowlist must drive run_worker with run_claude patched: first call posts the needs_tool hold and returns, second call receives the legacy allowlist and a reduced max_budget_usd; a third call never happens. Add ::test_respawn_skipped_when_budget_remainder_too_small.

SPEC v3 (2026-09-23 04:45) after spec review T-0912 (round 2; four points folded in, further review waived by the Planner, verdict set to approve):
- The needs_tool signal is a result-dict key: the worker posts bus_post_result(status="held", result={"reason": "needs_tool:<tool id>"}); a module constant spawn.NEEDS_TOOL_PREFIX = "needs_tool:" is the single source of the wording, and the four prompt files carry the same literal sentence ("post bus_post_result with status held and result reason needs_tool:<tool id>"); _hidden_tool_request reads bus.get(task_id)["result"]["reason"].
- Spend accounting: the first attempt's actual cost is r["output"].get("total_cost_usd", 0); both attempts' usage are summed and released once through the existing pool.release() call in run_worker's finally (additive usage dict), so reservation history and goal spend count both runs.
- Acceptance tests added: tests/test_spawn.py::test_escalation_stamps_tool_escalation_used_and_sums_usage (pipeline gains tool_escalation_used; the released usage equals attempt 1 + attempt 2); tests/test_context_scorecard.py::test_hidden_tool_recovery_rate_in_by_role_task_class.
